title: Capability["context"]() is the same compiler-recognized call as Capability.context() and charges the same nominal row
notes: specification/requirements.mdx:34: '`Capability.context()` MUST be an inherited, compiler-recognized call on subclasses of `Context`. It MUST return the receiving capability's instance type and add that class's nominal identity to the enclosing function's inferred `R` row.' :36: 'The receiver MUST identify a `Context` subclass strongly enough for the compiler to record its nominal key.' :80: 'When the compiler knows the complete closure, an unsatisfied capability MUST be a compile error.' A literal element access is the same member access as the dotted spelling: same resolved property symbol, same emitted call. A recognizer that tests only for a PropertyAccessExpression is recognition-by-syntactic-form, and the computed spelling escapes every rule it owns. REVIEW-fable-1.md F4 measured `Clock["context"]()` compiling and PANICKING AT RUNTIME on BOTH backends, which is why only a specification-derived case can hold this closed: the differential oracle is structurally blind to a defect the two implementations share. The declared messageContains is the capability's own name, for the reason 05-context-rows/an-unsatisfied-top-level-requirement-names-exactly-the-capability records: a refusal that names the WRONG requirement, or an empty row, satisfies a code-and-position expectation exactly.
